previewing-update-and-delete-targets.label: Previewing Mutation Targets
previewing-update-and-delete-targets.summary: Learn how to safely preview and execute SQL mutations by using SELECT statements to identify target rows before applying UPDATE or DELETE operations.

sketch1.title: Carry the Filter Into the Change

try_previewing_update_and_delete_targets.title: Preview Decor Test Rows
try_previewing_update_and_delete_targets.prompt: Before any cleanup is approved, inspect the Decor rows that are marked as test data. In `query.sql`, return all columns for only that target set.
try_previewing_update_and_delete_targets.hint: This is inspection only; do not mutate the table.

help.concept: A preview lets you validate a target set before any data-changing statement runs.
help.hint_1: Use the category and test flag together.

try_previewing_update_and_delete_targets.starterCode: -- Return the verification result required for "Preview Decor Test Rows" below.
try_previewing_update_and_delete_targets.solutionCode: SELECT * FROM inventory_items WHERE category = 'Decor' AND is_test = 1;

query_sql.content: -- Return the verification result required for "Preview Decor Test Rows" below.
SELECT * FROM inventory_items WHERE category = 'Decor' AND is_test = 1;

single-choice-preview.title: Why Preview Before Mutation?
single-choice-preview.prompt: Why is it important to preview rows with a SELECT statement before executing an UPDATE or DELETE?
single-choice-preview.hint: Consider the impact of unintended data changes.

help.concept: Previewing helps ensure only intended rows are affected by a mutation.
help.hint_1: Previewing prevents accidental changes to unintended rows.
help.hint_2: It allows you to verify the target set before making changes.

options.a: To ensure the SQL syntax is correct
options.b: To verify the target rows before making changes
options.c: To speed up the execution of the query

fill-blank-choice-update.title: Fill in the Blank: UPDATE Statement
fill-blank-choice-update.prompt: Complete the following UPDATE statement to change the status of all 'Kitchen' items to 'inactive'.
fill-blank-choice-update.hint: Read the sentence around the blank and decide what role the missing word plays.

help.concept: The blank should be filled with the term that makes the statement accurate.
help.hint_1: Look at the words before and after the blank to infer what kind of term is needed.
help.hint_2: Pick the choice that completes the statement with the clearest meaning.

fill-blank-choice-update.template: UPDATE inventory_items SET status = 'inactive' WHERE category = [blank1];

multi-choice-verify.title: What Successful Verification Confirms
multi-choice-verify.prompt: Which outcomes should a successful post-mutation verification confirm? Select all that apply.
multi-choice-verify.hint: Check both the intended target and rows that were supposed to stay untouched.

help.concept: Verification confirms the intended final values and protects against collateral changes outside the approved target set.
help.hint_1: Inspect the rows you meant to change.
help.hint_2: Also confirm that unrelated rows still look as expected.

options.a: The intended rows now have the approved values.
options.b: Every row in the table was changed.
options.c: Rows outside the target still have their expected values.
options.d: The SQL statement was shorter than the preview query.

drag-reorder-mutation-steps.title: Order the Verification Workflow
drag-reorder-mutation-steps.prompt: Arrange the steps for a reviewed UPDATE or DELETE from first action to final safety check.
drag-reorder-mutation-steps.hint: Begin with the read-only preview and end by checking rows outside the target.

help.concept: The workflow establishes the target, performs the approved mutation, verifies the changed rows, and then checks that unrelated rows stayed untouched.
help.hint_1: Start with “Preview target rows with SELECT”.
help.hint_2: Finish with “Check that unrelated rows stayed unchanged”.

tokens.t2: Execute the approved UPDATE or DELETE
tokens.t3: Re-run a SELECT for the changed rows
tokens.t4: Check that unrelated rows stayed unchanged

single-choice-where.title: Role of WHERE in Mutations
single-choice-where.prompt: What is the role of the WHERE clause in an UPDATE or DELETE statement?
single-choice-where.hint: Think about how WHERE affects the scope of the mutation.

help.concept: WHERE specifies which rows are affected by the mutation.
help.hint_1: WHERE limits the mutation to specific rows.
help.hint_2: Without WHERE, all rows could be affected.

options.a: It specifies the columns to update
options.b: It limits the rows affected by the mutation
options.c: It speeds up the query execution
options.d: It is optional in all mutations

practice-update-reviewed-target-set.title: Practice: Update a Reviewed Target Set
practice-update-reviewed-target-set.prompt: The pricing team approved a price of `10.99` for legitimate Accessories inventory. In `operations.sql`, use an `UPDATE` with a `WHERE` condition that limits the change to Accessories rows that are not test data. In `query.sql`, inspect the affected rows after the change. To test it in the workspace, run `operations.sql` before `query.sql`; the query file only reads the resulting database state.
practice-update-reviewed-target-set.hint: The approved target needs both the category and non-test conditions.

help.concept: A reviewed filter should remain the mutation's safety boundary.
help.hint_2: Verify only the reviewed target set.

practice-update-reviewed-target-set.starterCode: -- Apply the approved data change for "Update Approved Accessories" below.
practice-update-reviewed-target-set.solutionCode: UPDATE inventory_items SET price = 10.99 WHERE category = 'Accessories' AND is_test = 0;

query_sql.content: -- Return the verification result required for "Update Approved Accessories" below.

operations_sql.content: UPDATE inventory_items SET price = 10.99 WHERE category = 'Accessories' AND is_test = 0;

query_sql.content: SELECT * FROM inventory_items WHERE category = 'Accessories' AND is_test = 0;

preview-select.title: Preview the target set before changing it
preview-select.bodyMarkdown:
Before an `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, use a `SELECT` to inspect the rows that the business rule identifies.

```sql
SELECT *
FROM inventory_items
WHERE category = 'Kitchen';
```

If the preview contains an unexpected row, the mutation condition is not ready yet. Fix the scope before changing data.

mutation-execution.title: Carry the reviewed scope into the mutation
mutation-execution.bodyMarkdown:
Once the preview is correct, the mutation should preserve that same target boundary.

```sql
UPDATE inventory_items
SET status = 'active'
WHERE category = 'Kitchen';
```

The important workflow is: preview the intended set, apply the approved change to that set, then verify the resulting state.
